title: Philliberto: The Villain Who Keeps Showing Up in the Final Act
body: Every league needs a bad guy, and the Buckaroo Football League found its man on day one. Alan, known to friend and foe alike as Philliberto, Philly, or simply Phillibert, has run Team Pillbert since the league's founding in 2023 and has never once finished last. He has also never once lifted the Buckaroo Bowl, which is either the most frustrating or the most satisfying sentence on this website, depending on how you feel about him. Most of the league knows which way they lean.

The 2023 debut was a classic villain entrance. Team Pillbert went 9-5, scored 1,499.3 points, grabbed the 2 seed, and in week 3 dropped a career-best 156.2 on Sonny, a beatdown the commissioner surely remembers every time he checks the record book he built. Philly rode that form all the way to Buckaroo Bowl I, where Kaushal's Habibsters were waiting, and the bad guy finished 2nd of 6. Then came the slow fade: 6-8 in 2024 with a 4 seed and a 3rd-place finish, a season that included the 64.1-point faceplant against Kaushal in week 10 that ranks as his worst week ever.

2025 looked like the villain's downfall. Team Pillbert went 5-11 and limped in as the 6 seed, the bottom of the bracket, despite piling up a career-high 1,762.9 points, which suggests the schedule gods were rooting against him too. The low point may have been week 9, when Ramon's Remains, a team literally abandoned by its manager, edged him 94.76-92.02. Losing to a ghost ship is a special kind of humiliation. And yet, in true supervillain fashion, he climbed off the mat and finished 4th of 6, sending someone else down the consolation ladder instead.

The head-to-head ledger reads like a list of people Phillibert enjoys tormenting. He owns Randy 8-5, leads Mekhi 6-4 and Brucie 6-5, and is 1-0 against JMoney, though Sonny has him 6-5. The one hero who has his number is Habib: Kaushal leads the series 7-2, making the two-time champ Team Pillbert's true nemesis. As a manager, Philly started as a hoarder who never traded, with zero deals in 2023 and 2024, while his waiver activity climbed from 11 pickups to 21 to 25.

Which brings us to 2026, and a villain who has clearly been studying his own origin story. Team Pillbert is 5-1 with 731.6 points and a 27 percent shot at the title, powered by a man who has already made 4 trades this year after making 1 in his first three seasons combined, plus 16 pickups. The bad guy has rebuilt his lair, the rest of the league is nervously checking the standings, and his playoff record sits at 1-2. If Phillibert finally wins the Buckaroo Bowl, expect the league to treat it like the credits rolling with the villain on the throne.
